title: The sigma notation and partial sums
competency: Find partial sums and read and write sums in sigma notation.

keywords.def: Sₙ, the sum of the first n terms of a sequence.
The symbol ∑ for adding the terms aₖ from a lower to an upper limit.
The letter (like k) that runs from the lower to the upper limit.
The sum of the terms of a sequence.

en.text: A partial sum Sₙ adds the first n terms of a sequence: Sₙ = a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ. Some sums telescope: when each term is a difference like 1/n − 1/(n + 1), the middle parts cancel and only the first and last parts remain.

am.text: ከፊል ድምር Sₙ የመጀመሪያዎቹን n ተርሞች ይደምራል። አንዳንድ ድምሮች ይታጠፋሉ (ቴሌስኮፒንግ)፤ መካከለኛዎቹ ይሰረዛሉ።

screens.title: Add the first five
screens.after:
Add in order: 2 + 4 = 6, 6 + 6 = 12, 12 + 8 = 20, 20 + 10 = 30.
Or pair the ends: 2 + 10 = 12, 4 + 8 = 12, and 6 is left: 12 + 12 + 6 = 30.
Adding the first terms of a sequence gives a partial sum.

screens.title: Partial sums
paras: S₁ = a₁.  S₂ = a₁ + a₂.  S₃ = a₁ + a₂ + a₃.
Sₙ = a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ is the sum of the first n terms.
Sₙ is called the partial sum.

screens.title: Partial sums of the odd numbers
screens.ask: Tap ▶ to add one odd number at a time. Watch S₁, S₂, S₃, … grow.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Sₙ, the sum of the first n terms of a sequence.

screens.ask: Find the partial sum S₆ (the sum of the first 6 terms) of aₙ = 3n + 1: S₆ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: list a₁ to a₆: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19.
Step 2: pair the ends: 4 + 19 = 23, 7 + 16 = 23, 10 + 13 = 23.
Step 3: 3 pairs × 23 = 69.
So S₆ = 69. (Trap: a₆ = 19 is the 6th term, not the sum.)

screens.title: aₙ = 1/(n(n + 1)): the sum of 99 terms
steps: Each middle fraction appears with + and with −, so they cancel.

screens.ask: Find a partial sum: the sum of the first ten odd numbers is ___
screens.why:
Step 1: the first ten odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, …, 19.
Step 2: pair the ends: 1 + 19 = 20, 3 + 17 = 20, … : 5 pairs.
Step 3: 5 × 20 = 100.
Check: the sum of the first n odd numbers is n², and 10² = 100 ✓.
screens.clue: Pair the first and last terms.

screens.ask: Find the partial sum S₈ of aₙ = 3 − 5n: S₈ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: a₁ = 3 − 5 = −2 and a₈ = 3 − 40 = −37.
Step 2: the terms go down by 5, so pair the ends: −2 + (−37) = −39.
Step 3: 8 terms make 4 pairs: 4 × (−39) = −156.
So S₈ = −156.

screens.ask: Find the partial sum S₆ of aₙ = n² + 1: S₆ = ___

screens.text: Telescoping sum: find Sₙ for aₙ = 2/((n + 2)(n + 3)).
screens.clue: Split into two fractions. The first part left is 1/3.

screens.ask: Use the telescoping result Sₙ = n/(n + 1): find S₂₀ for aₙ = 1/(n(n + 1)). S₂₀ = ___

en.text: Sigma ∑ writes a long sum in short form. ∑ from k = m to n of aₖ means: put k = m, m + 1, …, n into aₖ and add. There are n − m + 1 terms. Renaming the index or shifting it carefully does not change the sum.

am.text: ሲግማ ∑ ረጅም ድምርን በአጭሩ ይጽፋል። ከ k = m እስከ n ያሉትን እሴቶች በ aₖ ውስጥ አስገብተን እንደምራለን። ተርሞቹ n − m + 1 ናቸው።

screens.title: A short way to write a sum
screens.after:
Write each term as 3 × k: 3 = 3 × 1, 6 = 3 × 2, …, 24 = 3 × 8.
k runs from 1 to 8, so there are 8 terms.
(24 is the last term, not the number of terms.)
Sigma writes this as ∑ₖ₌₁⁸ 3k.

screens.title: Sigma notation
paras: ∑ is the Greek capital letter sigma.
k is the index, 1 is the lower limit, n is the upper limit.

screens.title: Read the parts
items: The lower limit: the first value of k.
The upper limit: the last value of k.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The symbol ∑ for adding the terms aₖ from a lower to an upper limit.
The letter (like k) that runs from the lower to the upper limit.

screens.ask: Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₁⁸ 3k = ___

screens.title: ∑ₖ₌₂⁶ k²
steps: k starts at 2, not 1. So 1² is not included.

screens.why:
Step 1: ∑ₖ₌₃⁷ k²: k = 3 to 7 gives 3² to 7² ✓.
Step 2: ∑ᵢ₌₃⁷ i²: only the letter changes ✓.
Step 3: ∑ₖ₌₂⁶ (k + 1)²: k = 2 gives 3², k = 6 gives 7² ✓.
Step 4: ∑ₖ₌₁⁷ k² starts at 1², so it adds 1² + 2² extra ✗.
screens.clue: Write out the first and last term of each.

screens.ask: Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₃⁵ k³ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: k = 3, 4, 5: three terms.
Step 2: 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, 5³ = 125.
Step 3: 27 + 64 + 125 = 216.
So the sum is 216.

Step 1: the numbers squared are 2, 4, …, 12 = 2k for k = 1 to 6.
Step 2: so the sum is ∑ₖ₌₁⁶ (2k)².
Check k = 6: (12)² ✓.
(2k² squares only k: k = 2 gives 8, not 16. Upper limit 12 gives 12 terms.)
screens.clue: What is being squared each time?

screens.title: Match each sigma sum to its value
screens.text: Expand each sigma sum and match it to its value.
screens.clue: Write out every term first. Watch where k starts.

screens.ask: Count the terms in the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₄²⁰ (2k − 1): ___
screens.why:
Step 1: k runs 4, 5, …, 20.
Step 2: number of terms = upper − lower + 1.
Step 3: 20 − 4 + 1 = 17.
So there are 17 terms. (16 forgets the + 1; 20 counts from 1.)

items.ask: Find a partial sum: the sum of the first five odd natural numbers = ___
items.why:
Step 1: the first five odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
Step 2: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.
Check: 5² = 25 ✓.

items.ask: Find a partial sum: the sum of the first ten odd natural numbers = ___
items.why:
Step 1: 1, 3, 5, …, 19 (ten numbers).
Step 2: pair first and last: 1 + 19 = 20, five pairs.
Step 3: 5 × 20 = 100.
Check: 10² = 100 ✓.

items.ask: Find the partial sum S₅ of aₙ = 4n − 3: S₅ = ___
items.why:
Step 1: the terms are 1, 5, 9, 13, 17.
Step 2: pair the ends: 1 + 17 = 18, 5 + 13 = 18, and 9 is left.
Step 3: 18 + 18 + 9 = 45.
So S₅ = 45.

items.ask: Find the partial sum S₈ of aₙ = 3 − 5n: S₈ = ___
items.why:
Step 1: a₁ = −2, a₈ = −37.
Step 2: each pair of ends adds to −39.
Step 3: 8 terms = 4 pairs: 4 × (−39) = −156.

items.ask: Find the partial sum S₆ of aₙ = n² + 1: S₆ = ___

items.text: Telescoping sum: find Sₙ for aₙ = 2/(n² + 5n + 6).
items.why:
Step 1: factor: n² + 5n + 6 = (n + 2)(n + 3).
Step 2: split: aₙ = 2[1/(n + 2) − 1/(n + 3)].
Step 3: the middle terms cancel: Sₙ = 2[1/3 − 1/(n + 3)].
Step 4: = 2n/(3(n + 3)) = 2n/(3n + 9).
Check n = 1: 2/12 = 1/6 and 2/12 ✓.

items.ask: Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₁⁶ 2k = ___
items.why:
Step 1: k = 1 to 6: 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 + 12.
Step 2: pair the ends: 2 + 12 = 14, three pairs.
Step 3: 3 × 14 = 42.

items.ask: Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₃⁵ k² = ___
items.why:
Step 1: start at k = 3: 3², 4², 5².
Step 2: 9 + 16 + 25 = 50.
(Trap: starting at k = 1 adds 1 + 4 and gives 55.)

items.text: Write the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₁ⁿ 3ᵏ as a sum of terms.
items.why:
Step 1: k = 1 gives 3¹ = 3 (not 3⁰ = 1).
Step 2: k = 2 gives 9, k = 3 gives 27.
Step 3: the last value k = n gives 3ⁿ.
So 3 + 9 + 27 + … + 3ⁿ. (3 + 6 + 9 is 3k, not 3ᵏ.)

items.ask: Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₃⁵ k³ = ___

test.ask: Find the partial sum S₅ of aₙ = 4n − 3: S₅ = ___
Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₁⁶ 2k = ___
Expand and add the sigma sum ∑ₖ₌₂⁴ k² = ___
test.why:
k starts at 2: 2², 3², 4².
4 + 9 + 16 = 29.
(Starting at 1 would give 30.)

test.text: Sigma notation: which sum equals ∑ₖ₌₁⁵ k?
test.why:
∑ₖ₌₁⁵ k = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15.
∑ⱼ₌₁⁵ j is the same sum with a new letter: 15 ✓.
∑ₖ₌₀⁵ (k + 1) = 1 + … + 6 = 21. ∑ₖ₌₂⁶ k = 20. ∑ 2k = 30.
So ∑ⱼ₌₁⁵ j.
